newsitem.title: USA: U.S. whistleblower wins $8.4 million award.
newsitem.headline: U.S. whistleblower wins $8.4 million award.

text.p: An engineer who resigned from a nuclear-cleanup company saying it was guilty of fraud and wrongdoing has been awarded $8.4 million from the firm in a federal whistleblower settlement.
U.S. District Court Judge S. Arthur Spiegel on Thursday approved of the settlement reached by Fluor Daniel Fernald, the company, and William Watt, 59, Augusta, Georgia, the whistleblower.
When Watt resigned as a project control engineer in January 1995, he said he could no longer be associated with a company that practiced fraud and wrongdoing "on a regular basis."

In December 1993, he had filed a suit under the federeal law that protects and rewards whistleblowers alleging that Fluor Daniel Fernald, part of Fluor Daniel/GTI Inc. , had bilked taxpayers of more than $92 million in fraudulent charges in its cleanup of the former Fernald Atomic Energy plant near Cincinnati.
Fluor Daniel agreed to the settlement but did not admit any wrongdoing.
Company President John Bradbourne issued a news release which said, "We have vigorously investigated these claims, found no wrongdoing and spent nearly $2 million in our defence."
He said the company settled because it had become too costly to fight the case in court and had been too distracting to the firm's mission of a safe cleanup of the Fernald site.
If Fluor Daniel Fernald had lost the case in court, it could have been ordered to pay triple damages -- $276 million.
